definition: Loop unrolling is an optimization technique that involves duplicating the body of a loop a certain number of times, reducing the overhead of loop control and increasing the speed of the program.
details: Loop unrolling is an optimization technique that involves duplicating the body of a loop a certain number of times, reducing the overhead of loop control and increasing the speed of the program.

explainer.lead: A compiler optimisation that duplicates a loop body several times to cut loop-control overhead and speed up execution. It matters as a standard low-level performance technique.

tiers.eli5: Instead of checking the oven clock after every single cookie, you bake four at a time and check once.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply it via compilers or manually to hot loops; a pitfall is over-unrolling, which bloats code size and can hurt instruction-cache performance.
tiers.paperLevel: Duplicates the loop body a fixed number of times, reducing the overhead of loop control and increasing program speed.

explainer.example: A loop summing 1000 array elements is unrolled fourfold so each iteration adds four elements, cutting branch checks by roughly 75%.
